title: read through a pointer into a pool whose whole lifetime has ended
object: a, 24 bytes, never freed individually; st_alloc_fini releases the pool it lives in
note: The defect that exists BECAUSE of the custom allocator: PostgreSQL's MemoryContextReset, Apache's apr_pool_destroy, every arena's free-everything-at-end-of-request. st_alloc_fini runs here and again in harness/main.c, so every allocator must make it idempotent (alloc.h).

asan.why: The mirror image of case 8, and the cleanest asymmetry in the study: an arena HIDES accesses inside its pool and EXPOSES accesses after its pool, because the pool itself is one malloc block whose lifetime malloc-granular tools do see. No annotation needed, and the annotated arm adds nothing. malloc has no pool, so that column is UNSUPPORTED (see requires).

valgrind.why: Same: the pool block was freed. malloc has no pool (see requires).

hwasan.why: The pool's granules are retagged when the block is freed. HWASan has no public custom-allocator interface, so the annotated columns are UNSUPPORTED, not MISSED (C3.4).

ubsan.why: -fsanitize=bounds needs a statically known array bound; a pointer out of an allocator has none. The row is kept so the report can say UBSan is not a heap tool rather than leaving it out.

lowfat.why: LowFat checks bounds only; it has no notion of a lifetime.

status: written, smoke-run on malloc and arena; server run pending (A5)

requires.why: the allocator must carve from a pool whose lifetime st_alloc_fini ends. Under malloc st_alloc_fini is a no-op, the object stays live and the read is legitimate; that column is UNSUPPORTED by construction and the malloc equivalent is case 9.
